A 28 year old young man with blood in stools, SOB, fever and cough

  • Facebook

- August 21, 2022
This is an online E logbook to discuss our patient’s de-identified health data shared after taking his/her/guardian’s signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patient’s problems through a series of inputs from the available global online community of experts intending to solve those patients' clinical problems with collective current best evidence-based inputs

Chief complaint-
A 28 year old young man, a post graduate and resident of miryalaguda came to OPD with chief complaint of-
Blood in stools since 1½ yrs 
Fever and cough since a week,
Shortness of breath on exertion since 6 months

History of present illness-
Patient was asymptomatic 1½yr ago and then he noticed blood in stools monthly once or twice.
He had fever associated with dry cough since a week.
Fever subsided on medication and recurred later.
He went to a local hospital and was found to have low hemoglobin concentration and they suggested him colonscopy.
He came here for colonoscopy( gastroenterologist)
He was admitted here on 18/8/22 and transfused with a unit of blood and another unit on 19/8/22. 

History of past illness-
He had polio since he was 5 years old.
And had a surgery done on his left upper thigh region in 2009 at tirupathi hospital.

No history of HTN, Diabetes, Asthma

Family history-
Not significant 

Personal History-
Diet: mixed
Appetite: normal 
Bowel and bladder: regular
Sleep: adequate 
Addictions: none

General Examination-
Patient is concious, coherent and cooperative
Poorly built and moderately nourished
Pallor-present
No icterus
No cyanosis
No Clubbing of fingers
No Generalised lymphadenopathy 

Virals-
Temperature- 98⁰ F
Pulse rate- 89 bpm
Respiratory rate- 20 cpm
Blood pressure- 110/90 mmof Hg
SpO2- 98% at room air

Systemic examination-
Cardiovascular system-
S1 and S2 heard
no murmurs heard

Investigation-
18/8/22

19/8/22-

20/8/22

22/8/22
